findings.source_quote: ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα, ὃ ὁ Θεὸς κατῴκισεν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ταύτῃ, ἀληθὲς εὑρεθῇ παρὰ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις
findings.english_quote: Then the spirit which God has made to dwell in this flesh[h] may be found true before all people[g].
findings.issue: Replacing the ἵνα connection with a separate sentence beginning “Then” obscures the purpose/result relationship between speaking truth and the indwelling spirit being found true. The source explicitly connects this clause to the preceding instruction; the simplified text presents it primarily as a subsequent possibility.
findings.suggested_revision: Reconnect the clauses explicitly, for example: “Love truth[p], and let all truth come from your mouth, so that the spirit which God has made to dwell in this flesh[h] may be found true before all people[g].” This proposed replacement requires fresh review before adoption.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all five paragraphs of the selected Greek. The standard edition preserves the clauses, difficult assertions, negations, necessity, dialogue, and conditions. The simplified edition needs an explicit connection for the opening purpose/result clause. Both follow the current servant policy. Their witness notes are compatible with the supplied bounded reports, including distinctions between preserved text, supplied material, conjecture, mediated versions, and adapted quotation. Acceptance here concerns fidelity to the working source and supplied disclosures, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive scholarly collation.
